connections.observation: The framing pair ἅ τε λεκτέον καὶ ὡς λεκτέον at 392c and 398b encloses Socrates' prose rendering of Homer at 393d–394a. Socrates performs ὡς λεκτέον (simple narration ἄνευ μέτρου) within the very section bounded by the announced inquiry into ἅ τε and ὡς. The disclaimer οὐ γάρ εἰμι ποιητικός marks the enacted conversion from mimetic to simple mode.

The μιμ- family (s001) and διήγησις (s002) recur throughout; then at 394c the genre cluster (s006) distributes them: tragedy and comedy are διὰ μιμήσεως ὅλη, dithyramb διʼ ἀπαγγελίας, epic διʼ ἀμφοτέρων. The recurrent lexical density resolves into a threefold poetic taxonomy that applies the terms to named forms.

Socrates calls himself γελοῖος and ἀσαφής (s008) after Adeimantus requests σαφέστερον μαθεῖν; the μανθάνω series (s003) then tracks Adeimantus' repeated failures and eventual comprehension. The self-deprecating teacher and the struggling learner are grammatically enacted: imperative μάνθανε immediately follows declarative μανθάνω, μαθεῖν, μανθάνεις across the section.

The poet ὁμοιοῦν ἑαυτὸν versus ἀποκρύπτοιτο ὁ ποιητής (s007) is demonstrated in the Chryses passage (s009, s010). Homer hides himself and becomes Chryses (ὡς αὐτὸς ὢν ὁ Χρύσης); Socrates reveals the poet and keeps Chryses as reported object (ἦλθεν ὁ Χρύσης, ἐλθὼν ὁ ἱερεύς). The theorized contrast between concealment and likeness is enacted in consecutive retellings.

The one-practice principle (ἓν ἐπιτήδευμα, πολλὰ δʼ οὔ, s011) applied to the guardians (s021) yields the rejection of the διπλοῦς or πολλαπλοῦς man (s019). The argument moves from an abstract claim about mimetic capacity through the guardians' specific role to a constitutional principle: ἕκαστος ἓν πράττει excludes the versatile imitator from the city.

Mimesis settles into ἔθη, φύσιν, σῶμα, φωνάς, διάνοιαν (s013); then the catalogue of sounds—thunder, winds, axles, pipes, animals (s014)—becomes what the inferior imitator's φωναί reproduce. The tripartite anthropology (body, voice, mind) is concretely filled by the accumulation of φωναί and φθόγγοι the multiform mimic performs.

The versatile poet is ἱερὸν καὶ θαυμαστὸν καὶ ἡδύν (s015), crowned and anointed, yet sent away; the austere poet chosen is ἀηδέστερος (s016). The section holds together reverence and expulsion: the most pleasant (ἥδιστος) is honored as sacred yet excluded, while the unpleasant (ἀηδέστερος) remains for ὠφελίας ἕνεκα.

The mixed poet (κεκραμένος, s017) is rejected in favor of the unmixed (ἄκρατον); the city excludes the διπλοῦς or πολλαπλοῦς man (s019). Mixing vocabulary applied to poetic modes corresponds to the constitutional exclusion of duplicity: the κεκραμένος poet is the πολλαπλοῦς man.

The tripled syntactic pattern (σκυτοτόμον σκυτοτόμον, γεωργὸν γεωργὸν, πολεμικὸν πολεμικὸν, s018) enacts ἕκαστος ἓν πράττει; the guardians (s021) are ἀφειμένους τῶν ἄλλων πασῶν δημιουργιῶν yet δημιουργοὺς ἐλευθερίας (s022). The repetition performs singularity of practice, while the paradox of being released from all δημιουργίαι to become δημιουργοὶ ἐλευθερίας holds the guardians' unique craft visible.

The virtues to be imitated—ἀνδρείους, σώφρονας, ὁσίους, ἐλευθέρους (s023)—frame what the μέτριος ἀνήρ (s024) will imitate without shame (οὐκ αἰσχυνεῖσθαι, s025); the worse he will not imitate, being ashamed (αἰσχυνεῖσθαι). Virtue, moderation, and shame converge: the measured man's selective mimesis is governed by what he can perform without αἰσχύνη.

The λόγος/λέξις distinction (s004) opens the inquiry; later, λόγος itself becomes πνεῦμα (s020) carrying the inquiry where it will. The formal object of investigation (λέξις) is separated from content (λόγος), yet λόγος as argument is compared to wind—the controlling term becomes an uncontrolled force within the section.

The genre cluster (s006) names τραγῳδία, κωμῳδία, διθύραμβος, ἔπη, ῥαψῳδοί, ὑποκριταί; Socrates converts Homeric ἔπη into prose ἄνευ μέτρου (s012), disclaiming being ποιητικός. The epic form named in the taxonomy is transformed into the mode the section theorizes (ἁπλῆ διήγησις), making the theorized category and the enacted speech momentarily identical.

σμικρὸν δέ τι μέρος ἐν πολλῷ λόγῳ τῆς μιμήσεως

new_signals.observation: λόγος recurs in four distinct senses: content (392c), argument as wind (394d), prior argument to preserve (395b), and extended speech (396e). The term shifts role across the section, from finished topic to moving force to normative reference to quantitative measure.

elements.context: Multiple occurrences of this brief question throughout the section

new_signals.observation: The phrase ἢ οὔ; recurs as a rhythmic punctuation throughout the dialogue, often receiving the answer πάνυ μὲν οὖν, ἔφη or similar brief affirmation. The repeated question-answer pair creates a percussive pattern of assent structuring the section's forward movement.

elements.context: τῷ αὐστηροτέρῳ καὶ ἀηδεστέρῳ ποιητῇ χρῴμεθα καὶ μυθολόγῳ ὠφελίας ἕνεκα

new_signals.observation: The austere and unpleasant poet is chosen ὠφελίας ἕνεκα—for the sake of benefit. This singular phrase names the ground for reversing the preference for pleasure (ἡδύς, ἥδιστος) by subordinating it to ὠφελία.

elements.context: ὃς ἡμῖν τὴν τοῦ ἐπιεικοῦς λέξιν μιμοῖτο

new_signals.observation: At 397d Adeimantus chooses τὸν τοῦ ἐπιεικοῦς μιμητὴν ἄκρατον; at 398b the chosen poet μιμοῖτο τὴν τοῦ ἐπιεικοῦς λέξιν. The phrase τοῦ ἐπιεικοῦς recurs in genitive across the two passages: first naming the unmixed imitator of the decent man, then naming the decent man's λέξις as object of imitation.
